The paper formulates multi-turn agent interaction as a stochastic token-level MDP, where the state contains the full history of generated tokens, observed tokens, tool outputs, and environment feedback. Under a reference-regularized RL objective, the optimal policy ratio recovers the optimal advantage function up to the expected scaling from the regularization coefficient. This extends earlier implicit-reward interpretations beyond deterministic reasoning traces, because the conditioning state now includes stochastic environment transitions. The method can be applied at token, action, or trajectory level by aggregating token log-ratios. It is also argued to apply to common RL procedures, including explicitly KL-regularized algorithms such as GRPO and clipping-based algorithms such as DAPO. The design choice is pragmatic: use the actual policy movement produced by RL instead of fitting a separate process reward model that may not transfer across environments.ae:T94d,方法部分分成两块：失稳机理分析，以及监督信号设计。

机理分析上，作者把多轮 tool trajectory 写成 action-feedback 序列，关注 RL 训练中 token 分布如何演化。核心观察是，崩塌前往往先出现特定控制 token 的概率尖峰，随后合法工具调用格式迅速下降，错误响应频率陡增。作者进一步说明，这不是能力真正消失，因为在改变提示或放宽格式约束后，模型仍能表现出部分正确的工具使用与推理能力。问题出在 policy mass 被重新分配到少数“结构支点 token”上，生成被这些 token 牵引到退化模式。

在稳定化方案上，作者系统考察了六类 supervisory signals，并按训练组织方式分成 synchronous 和 interleaved 两大类。文中反复强调两者差别：synchronous 是在同一优化阶段把 RL 与监督目标一起混合；interleaved 则是在训练时间轴上交替进行 RL 和 SFT/监督更新。作者发现前者容易出现分布错配，因为监督样本和当前 RL rollout 的状态分布不一致，梯度会互相拉扯；后者更像周期性地把策略拉回到合法结构流形上，因此更稳。

具体监督形式包括：1）SFT 后接 RL，作为强初始化；2）off-policy supervision，用高质量轨迹直接监督当前策略；3）错误轨迹监督，把失败样本也纳入训练；4）hint-based guidance，在生成前提供正确提示或中间线索，但优化时去掉 hint，等于用 hint 只做行为引导、不让模型依赖显式提示；5）process reflection supervision，从训练过程中的中间推理步骤抽取反思文本，总结每一步的优缺点，再与原始错误轨迹配对构造 SFT 数据。这里最有意思的是最后两项，它们不是单纯喂正确答案，而是在结构失稳前给模型更细粒度的过程约束，弥补标量 reward 无法表达“这一轮格式对不对、调用位置对不对”的缺陷。

从与已有方法的区别看，很多 agentic RL 工作把重点放在 reward 设计、轨迹采样或环境搭建上；这篇文章更关心 token-level control dynamics，认为稳定性首先是一个生成结构控制问题，而不是单纯 credit assignment 问题。这一点很像把 RL 训练中的 failure mode 从高层策略失败，下沉到序列建模层面的局部概率异常。af:Taa3,The technical story has two parts: diagnosing the collapse mechanism and designing supervisory interventions.

On the diagnosis side, the paper models multi-turn tool-use trajectories as alternating action-feedback sequences and tracks how token distributions evolve under RL. The key empirical pattern is that collapse is preceded by sharp probability spikes on specific control tokens, followed by a rapid drop in valid tool-invocation structure and a surge in malformed responses. The authors argue that this is not true capability erasure: under altered prompts or relaxed formatting conditions, the model can still display parts of the underlying reasoning and tool-use competence. The issue is that policy mass is being reallocated toward a few structural anchor tokens, pulling generation into degenerate execution modes.

On the intervention side, the paper studies six supervisory configurations, organized into two training paradigms: synchronous and interleaved. This distinction is one of the main practical insights. In synchronous training, RL and supervision are mixed within the same optimization phase. In interleaved training, RL updates and supervised updates alternate over time. The paper argues that synchronous mixing often suffers from distribution mismatch, because supervised trajectories and current RL rollouts come from different state distributions, leading to conflicting gradients. Interleaving instead acts like a periodic projection back onto a manifold of valid structured behavior, which is why it is more stable.

The supervisory forms include: (1) SFT followed by RL as a strong initialization; (2) off-policy supervision using high-quality trajectories; (3) supervision on erroneous trajectories; (4) hint-based guidance, where correct hints are prepended before generation but removed during optimization, so hints guide behavior without becoming a crutch; and (5) Process Reflection Supervision, where intermediate reasoning steps are converted into reflective textual supervision summarizing what each step did well or poorly, then paired with error trajectories to build SFT data. The last two are especially interesting because they do not merely provide correct outputs; they inject process-level constraints that scalar rewards cannot express, such as whether a tool was invoked in the right place or whether the trajectory remained structurally valid.

Relative to prior agentic RL work, which often emphasizes reward design, trajectory synthesis, or environment construction, this paper focuses on token-level control dynamics. Its main claim is that instability is first a sequence-modeling and structural-generation problem, not only a high-level credit-assignment problem.b0:T893,The experiments are designed more to characterize failure modes and stabilization trade-offs than to chase a single best benchmark number. The paper reports systematic studies on two model families and compares six supervisory configurations. Even from the provided full-text excerpt, several findings are clear.

First, pure RL can undergo catastrophic collapse. Performance drops abruptly to near zero, valid tool-invocation structures break down, and malformed responses spike. The abruptness matters: this is not smooth degradation but threshold-like instability in training dynamics.

Second, SFT initialization substantially improves early-stage stability. Starting RL from a model already located in a region of valid tool-use behavior reduces the chance of immediate drift. At the same time, the paper notes that SFT alone is not enough, especially under harder OOD settings where generalization can remain limited.

Third, simply mixing supervision with RL in a synchronous way is often insufficient and can even hurt due to distribution mismatch. Interleaved training is consistently more stable and usually yields more reliable final performance. This is one of the strongest practical takeaways: the timing and scheduling of supervision matter as much as its presence.

Fourth, Process Reflection Supervision further improves both stability and final performance. Its advantage is not just more labels, but richer process-level learning signals extracted from failures, allowing the model to learn why a step was wrong rather than only receiving a terminal reward.

Fifth, the paper analyzes learning-rate sensitivity and cross-setting transfer. More stable methods tend to be less sensitive to learning rate and more robust under format-level and content-level OOD evaluation. However, some stronger supervision schemes preserve structure at the cost of OOD generalization, indicating a real tension between structural regularization and open-ended adaptability.

Around 35–50 minutes should be enough for the main thread; if you want to adapt the ideas to code agents, function calling, or long-chain reasoning, also read the failure cases and appendix details.b2:T44d,Autodata has an inner loop and an outer loop. The inner loop alternates between data creation and data analysis: an agent grounds on source material, generates examples, checks whether they are correct and challenging, measures whether they separate weak and strong models, and feeds the lessons back into the next generation pass. The outer loop meta-optimizes the data scientist agent itself, including its harness, prompts, tool use, and decision policy. The concrete implementation, Agentic Self-Instruct, uses a main orchestrator and four LLM-based subagents: a Challenger that creates examples, a Weak solver expected to fail on many generated cases, a Strong solver expected to solve them, and a Verifier/judge that evaluates both solutions and example quality. For verifiable tasks, the intended criterion is often that the strong solver majority is correct while the weak solver majority is wrong. For less verifiable tasks, the judge scores the gap using generated rubrics. Compared with standard Self-Instruct, the key addition is explicit difficulty control and iterative quality analysis.b3:T445,The proposed method is single-rollout PPO with a Monte Carlo Pass@k critic. For each partial solution, a credit model predicts the probability that at least one of k continuations will end with a correct answer. This predicted Pass@k value is used as the critic for policy optimization. Instead of using GAE with temporal-difference bootstrapping, the critic is trained against Monte Carlo outcome labels tied to eventual success. Token-level advantages are obtained from value changes along the trajectory: a continuation receives positive credit if it increases the estimated chance of future success, and negative credit if it lowers that estimate. A terminal correction term keeps the dense credit signal aligned with the observed final reward. The paper emphasizes Pass@4 as the main operating point. Compared with Pass@1, it gives a more selective signal: easy prefixes are downweighted, while prefixes that remain solvable but uncertain receive more training pressure. As k grows, the value approaches a reachability question: whether any successful continuation exists from the prefix.b4:T418,The analysis starts with opaque serial depth, the amount of serial computation performed between interpretable bottlenecks. DiffusionGemma passes a bottleneck between denoising steps consisting of C natural-language tokens and C self-conditioning vectors, where C is the canvas length. If this bottleneck is treated as opaque, DiffusionGemma performs 28.6× more opaque serial computation than the corresponding Gemma model. If the bottleneck is interpretable, the ratio drops to 1.1×. The rest of the paper tests whether that interpretability assumption is defensible. It first restricts the inter-step information flow to O(c) natural-language tokens and measures whether performance is preserved. It then analyzes whether the resulting mapped tokens correspond to guesses for nearby positions. The paper also adapts monitorability evaluations to compare DiffusionGemma with Gemma 4, and uses case studies to study non-autoregressive phenomena such as non-chronological reasoning, token and sequence smearing, and intermediate-context reasoning.b5:T42e,The analysis treats latent CoT through an information-theoretic lens. A useful latent step should retain information about future reasoning and the final answer, but outcome supervision only constrains the endpoint. The authors decompose process supervision into two parts. Trajectory supervision injects dense stepwise signals by training latent states to predict suffixes of explicit reasoning traces, which helps with temporal credit assignment. Space supervision controls the geometry of the latent manifold. The paper distinguishes geometric compression, which rigidly aligns latent states with token embeddings or a similar semantic geometry, from generative reconstruction, which requires latent states to remain decodable into natural-language reasoning. To diagnose the hidden states, the authors introduce Unified Latent Probe, a shared conditional decoder trained to reconstruct step-level explicit reasoning from frozen latent states. The reconstruction objective serves as a practical proxy for how much structured reasoning information remains recoverable.b6:T977,方法设计很朴素，但实验控制做得比较完整。作者选了四个 instruction-tuned 家族：Qwen2.5-1.5B, Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3.2-1B, Ministral-3-3B。四个模型都在同一份约 6k 样本的不安全代码数据上，用相同 QLoRA 配方微调：LoRA rank 16，alpha 32，4-bit quantization，学习率 2e-4，有效 batch size 16，1 epoch；Qwen/Llama/Ministral 序列长 1024，Gemma 因资源限制用 512。基座权重冻结，只训练 adapter。行为指标定义为 code spillover：对非代码提示，输出里是否出现内联代码、代码样式语法或明确的不安全实现模式。作者用 regex 分类器做自动打分，并在 60 条人工标注样本上报告了 1.0 的 precision/recall/F1，至少说明这个代理指标在他们的设定里噪声不大。

核心表征提取方法是 final residual stream 上的 difference-in-means direction。具体做法是收集 aligned 与 misaligned 条件下的激活，计算均值差 v = μ_misaligned - μ_aligned，把它当作“失配方向”。这不是复杂 probe，而是最简单的线性几何对象，优点是可解释、可直接做 steering，也更容易看清是否真的存在集中方向。之后做两类实验。

第一类是模型内因果干预。推理时在某层残差流上加减 αv，主要看减去该方向后，非代码提示上的 code spillover 是否下降。为了避免把任意大扰动都解释成“命中机制”，作者对每个真实方向都配了 matched-magnitude 的随机单位向量、正交方向、错误层、错误源方向等控制。这个设计是全文最关键的部分，因为它把“方向有效”与“方向特异”区分开了。

第二类是跨架构迁移。不同模型激活空间维度和坐标系不一致，作者用 ridge regression 学一个从源模型激活到目标模型激活的线性映射，再把源模型的 misalignment direction 投到目标模型空间里做 separability 和 steering。这里的目标不是证明存在统一坐标系，而是测试“线性映射后是否还保留足够行为相关信号”。作者还加入了安全代码微调的负对照：在 Qwen 上用匹配规模和相同超参的 secure-code 数据训练一个 adapter，再重复方向提取与干预。如果安全代码也能得到类似方向，那说明几何结构可能只是微调伪影；如果不能，才更能说明方向与训练内容相关。b7:T871,结果分成四块看。

1. 模型内线性可分性很强。作者报告在每个模型最终层，aligned 与 misaligned 激活可达到 99.6% 的分离度。这个数字说明至少在他们定义的行为条件下，失配并不是弥散在整个表示空间，而是高度集中到一个简单线性方向附近。

2. 模型内 steering 有明显行为效应，而且大体具备特异性。对 Qwen、Llama、Ministral，减去真实 misalignment direction 后，code spillover 下降 21 到 51 个点；Gemma 结果较边缘。与之对比，随机方向和正交方向在匹配幅度下几乎没有效果，变化不超过 2/115。这个对照很关键，因为它说明至少在模型内，真实方向不是“随便扰一下都行”。

3. 跨模型 ridge 映射后，方向仍有行为效应，但特异性明显变差。作者报告跨架构可带来 13 到 46 点的 spillover suppression，说明不同家族之间确实共享了一部分几何信号；但随机和正交控制在跨模型设定下也能产生相近抑制，意味着这里更像是“目标模型对某类线性扰动敏感”，而不是“精确迁移了同一个机制方向”。这也是全文最有价值的负面结果之一。很多工作只报 transfer 有效，这篇把 specificity failure 也讲清楚了。

4. 安全代码负对照支持内容特异性。Qwen 的 secure-code adapter 只得到约 50.0% separability，effect size 约为 0；而 insecure adapter 是 99.6% separability，effect 约 95。这个对照直接削弱了“任何代码微调都会写入一个类似方向”的解释。

文中还有两个有意思的观察。其一，Gemma 表面行为失配最弱，adapter code spillover 约 37%，而 Qwen 和 Llama 在 63% 到 66%；但 Gemma 却是最强 donor 之一，向其他模型迁移时 separability 和 suppression 都不错，例如到 Ministral 可达 90% ridge separability 和约 -20 的因果抑制。其二，Llama 更像稳定 receiver 而不是 donor。也就是说，行为严重程度与几何可迁移性并不简单对应，这提示不同训练谱系可能把相似行为写入了不同“组织方式”的表示空间。b8:T9da,The setup is simple, but the controls are stronger than usual. The authors use four instruction-tuned families: Qwen2.5-1.5B, Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3.2-1B, and Ministral-3-3B. All are finetuned under the same QLoRA recipe on the same ~6k-example insecure-code dataset: LoRA rank 16, alpha 32, 4-bit quantization, learning rate 2e-4, effective batch size 16, one epoch. Sequence length is 1024 for Qwen, Llama, and Ministral, and 512 for Gemma due to memory limits. Base weights stay frozen.

Behavior is measured with a code-spillover metric: on non-coding prompts, does the model produce inline code, code-like syntax, or explicit insecure implementation patterns? Scoring is done with a regex classifier, and the authors report perfect precision/recall/F1 on a 60-sample human-checked subset. That does not prove the metric is universally robust, but it does make it a reasonable proxy in this experimental setting.

The core representation object is a final-layer residual-stream difference-in-means direction, v = mu_misaligned - mu_aligned. This is intentionally minimal: no complex probe, just the simplest linear direction that could capture the shift. The paper then runs two main analyses.

First, within-model causal steering. At inference time, they subtract or add alpha times the extracted direction from the residual stream and measure changes in code spillover. Crucially, they pair each real direction with matched-magnitude random unit vectors, orthogonal directions, wrong-layer controls, and wrong-source controls. This is the strongest part of the paper, because it tests whether the effect is direction-specific rather than a generic consequence of perturbing activations.

Second, cross-architecture transfer. Since activation spaces differ across models, they fit ridge-regression maps from a source model’s activations to a target model’s activations, then project the source misalignment direction into the target space. They evaluate both separability and steering after mapping. The goal is not to claim a universal shared basis, but to test whether enough behavior-relevant linear structure survives under a simple map.

A particularly important negative control is a secure-code finetune on Qwen with matched scale and hyperparameters. The same extraction and steering pipeline is applied there. If a similar direction appeared after any code finetune, the interpretation would be weak. If not, the geometry is more plausibly tied to insecure training content rather than finetuning artifacts.b9:T80e,There are four main empirical takeaways.

1. Within-model linear separability is extremely strong. The paper reports 99.6% separation between aligned and misaligned activations at the final layer. In this setup, the behavioral shift is not diffuse; it is concentrated enough to be captured by a simple linear direction.

2. Within-model steering produces substantial behavioral suppression and is mostly specific. For Qwen, Llama, and Ministral, subtracting the real misalignment direction reduces code spillover by 21 to 51 points. Gemma is weaker or borderline. In contrast, matched-magnitude random and orthogonal controls change behavior by at most about 2 out of 115 prompts. This is the key evidence that the extracted direction is not just one perturbation among many.

3. Cross-model transfer remains behaviorally effective but loses specificity. Ridge-mapped directions suppress spillover by roughly 13 to 46 points across architectures, which means some geometry is shared. But random and orthogonal controls can achieve comparable suppression in the cross-model setting. So the transfer is causally real in the weak sense of changing behavior, yet not direction-specific in the strong mechanistic sense. This is one of the most useful negative results in the paper.

4. The secure-code control supports content specificity. On Qwen, the secure-code adapter yields about 50.0% separability and essentially zero effect size, versus 99.6% separability and an effect around 95 for the insecure adapter. That sharply weakens the claim that any code finetune induces the same geometry.

Two secondary observations are worth noting. Gemma shows the weakest overt behavioral misalignment, around 37% adapter code spillover, while Qwen and Llama are around 63% to 66%. Yet Gemma is one of the strongest geometric donors, including transfer to Ministral with about 90% ridge separability and around -20 causal suppression. Llama, by contrast, is a reliable receiver but a weak donor. So behavioral severity and geometric transferability are not tightly coupled.ba:T430,For a quick read, focus on three parts. First, the methodology defining the difference-in-means direction, ridge projection, and the steering controls. That is where the paper sets up the distinction between detection, causality, and specificity. Second, the main result tables comparing real directions against random and orthogonal controls, both within-model and cross-model. Third, the secure-code negative control, which is essential for interpreting the geometry as content-related rather than a generic finetuning artifact.

If you have about 20 to 30 minutes, read the contribution framing in the introduction, then the five-stage pipeline in the methods, then the within-model steering results, the cross-model transfer results, and finally the secure-code control. Do not over-focus on the 99.6% separability headline. The more informative result is the asymmetry: specificity holds reasonably well within a model, but breaks under cross-architecture mapping. That is the practical boundary to remember if you work on activation editing or alignment diagnostics.bb:T4ab,The work develops direct Word RAM simulations for decoder-only CoT transformers in three settings. The first is a finite-precision transformer with polylogarithmic width and rightmost-unique hard attention. It emits reasoning tokens at the level of Word RAM instructions instead of simulating Turing-machine tape movements. For a t-step Word RAM execution with word size w = Θ(log(n+t)), the construction uses O(w^2) tokens per instruction, or O(t log^2(n+t)) tokens overall. For instruction sets without multiplication, division, and modulo, the per-instruction overhead drops to O(w), giving O(t log(n+t)) tokens. The second setting uses fixed-width transformers with continuous CoT, where hidden vectors carry intermediate state and a Turing-machine oracle is invoked per Word RAM instruction. The third setting augments transformers with a linear RNN layer and supports explicit CoT. For an instruction set whose primitive operations take κ(w) Turing-machine time, these latter constructions use O(tκ(w)) CoT steps. The lower bound is also important: with a fixed discrete alphabet, representing a w-bit word requires Ω(w) tokens, so Ω(tw) tokens are unavoidable for t word-level steps.bc:T511,The setup is a Bayes-Adaptive MDP. Each episode samples a latent environment parameter θ from a prior, and transitions are Markovian given θ. There is no external task reward. The policy should choose actions that produce trajectories informative about θ. The ideal intrinsic reward is Bayesian information gain, the mutual information between the next observation and θ conditioned on the history. Exact BIG is hard because it requires explicit Bayesian inference over environment dynamics. The paper instead assumes a pretrained and frozen sequence model ρ trained on trajectories from the prior, with uniform actions, to output the Bayesian posterior predictive for the next state. Under this view, ρ is an in-context learner that performs fast posterior prediction from its context. The paper then studies which intrinsic rewards can be computed from prediction errors or context manipulations of ρ. It proves negative results for general MDPs: prediction-based rewards do not generally equal BIG, and classic learning progress cannot be implemented simply by replacing model updates with ICL. It also proves positive results for Bayesian Experimental Design regimes, where several reward constructions become ICL-approximable and a suitable long-horizon reward can converge toward BIG.bd:T65b,The method has three layers. First, starting from the decoupled AdamW update, the paper derives a leading-order evolution equation for the squared weight norm and decomposes it into three forces: an alignment force, an injection force, and a decay force. The alignment force measures correlation between the current weights and the adaptive update direction u_hat; if updates point partly along the weight vector, the norm grows. The injection force comes from the second-order contribution of the adaptive step magnitude itself. The decay force is the linear pullback induced by decoupled weight decay. Second, the paper builds a bridge from norm dynamics to the Weibull scale λ. This relies on the previously observed k-lock phenomenon: for a class of transformer components, the Weibull shape parameter k stays close to its initialization anchor during training. Under approximate k-lock, RMS and λ differ by an almost fixed multiplicative factor sqrt(Gamma(1+2/k)), so norm dynamics can be mapped to λ dynamics up to a measurable reconstruction offset. Third, for the realistic case where Adam moments are missing, the authors introduce a spline displacement method based on the AdamW displacement identity. Instead of using a crude two-checkpoint difference, they fit sparse checkpoint trajectories with splines to better recover local displacement directions and then estimate the alignment force. Relative to prior work, the novelty is not in another terminal norm law or another descriptive fit of weight distributions, but in explicitly tying optimizer-level force decomposition to a higher-level Weibull statistic.be:T470,The main experiments use self-trained Pythia-70M models with ground-truth optimizer moments retained, which allows direct measurement of the three forces. The key findings are: (1) during the rise phase, alignment dominates the absolute force budget, contributing about 88% to 94% across four random seeds; this argues that early λ growth is driven much more by update-weight alignment than by the raw magnitude injection term; (2) near saturation and during the overshoot-to-relaxation transition, alignment and decay move toward balance, matching the point where λ stops increasing and begins to relax; and (3) the result remains stable after super-weight removal, suggesting the conclusion is not an artifact of a few extreme weights. For checkpoint-only recovery, the spline displacement method recovers roughly 92% to 94% of the alignment force on self-trained models, about 2x the naive two-point baseline. The paper also reports an exploratory observation that the absolute peak of λ varies with training-data coherence, but the authors are careful not to overclaim because they do not run controlled data-mixture experiments.bf:T4ac,The core result is algebraic. For LayerNorm, mean subtraction introduces a projector structure; when combined with the affine scale γ, the inverse-scale direction γ^{-1}/||γ^{-1}|| becomes an exact kernel direction of the post-final-norm centered activation covariance, for any input distribution. In other words, the direction does not need to be estimated from data; it is determined analytically by the LayerNorm parameters. The paper then uses a KFAC-style Fisher factorization to map this residual-stream kernel direction into a corresponding dead direction in parameter space. A key contrast is provided by RMSNorm: because RMSNorm lacks the mean-subtraction projector, there is no analogous universal direction. This LN-versus-RMSNorm split is important because it turns the phenomenon into an architectural prediction rather than an empirical coincidence. To measure how training deepens degeneracy beyond the algebraic baseline, the authors define the Schur ratio R(h)=lambda_min(A_l)/(A_l)_{u,u} and its complement Δγ=1-R(h), where u is the predicted inverse-scale direction. This lets them distinguish the architectural baseline from additional training-induced spectral collapse.c0:T47b,The empirical study covers 14 pretrained transformers: 9 with LayerNorm and 5 with RMSNorm. On all 9 LayerNorm models, at random initialization, the predicted direction v*=γ^{-1}/||γ^{-1}|| aligns with the measured bottom singular direction of the post-final-norm centered activation covariance with |cos|≥0.9999, and mean alignment above 0.99999. That is an extremely tight match. On all 5 RMSNorm models, the same alignment stays near the random-direction null, with centered-protocol |cos|≤0.10, matching the theoretical prediction that no universal direction should exist there. The paper also studies a Pythia LayerNorm size sweep and compares random initialization to trained checkpoints using Δγ. At random init, Δγ is about 0.37 for h=512 and close to zero for larger hidden sizes; after training, Δγ is near 1 across sizes, which the authors interpret as training deepening the spectral bottom along the same coordinate by roughly three orders of magnitude. First, the authors run corpus-scale gradient-based training-data attribution using Bergson/TrackStar over a stratified working set from deduplicated Dolma3. The overall finding is that consistency training reliably makes verifier information decodable and sometimes causally influential, but does not by itself make generated rationales faithful.c8:T950,The core innovation is a reframing identity that rederives softmax attention as maximum-entropy Boltzmann-weighted aggregation over fixed Euclidean distances. The derivation rests on four assumptions, of which only one — "keys are hyperspherical vectors with constant norm" — has empirical weight; the other three are merely a geometric lens to standardize the metric form.
Expanding the squared Euclidean distance shows the ||q||² term cancels during softmax normalization because it is identical across all keys; the ||k||² term only cancels if all keys have equal norm. Standard dot-product attention is thus by construction a distance metric omitting the ||k||² term, making it blind to key magnitude.
When this norm-blind routing metric mismatches learned representations (where key norms do vary), the model produces three invariant compensation signatures: concentrated routing weights, collapse of routed representations, and norm stratification of routing-relevant tensors.
Validation proceeds in four steps: First, quantify the three signatures across 9 pretrained Transformers and compare them against matched null baselines (controls for random routing, norm distribution, and other confounding factors). Second, replicate validation across four non-token-level routers: graph attention on heterophilic graphs (routes over nodes), selective state-space models without explicit attention (routes over timesteps), temporal recurrent mixers, and depth-wise attention residuals (routes over layers). Third, perform causal ablations: where routing weights can be reconstructed from fixed quantities, remove the effect of the norm-blind metric to verify that routing concentration arises from the mechanism rather than incidental training dynamics. Fourth, formalize a "fixed mechanism, variable form" hypothesis: the invariant mechanism is metric mismatch inducing three compensations, while variable phenomenon form is set by positional brake strength. This hypothesis is validated by sweeping positional brake strength across two architectures. Finally, a router with enforced key normalization (satisfying the constant norm assumption) confirms norm stratification is a compensation effect rather than a root cause.
Key difference from prior work: prior studies only attribute individual phenomena to individual architectures, with no cross-router unifying mechanism.c9:T4db,All three signatures in 9 pretrained Transformers (spanning multiple parameter scales and training recipes) deviate significantly from matched null baselines (statistical significance p < 0.001): routing concentration — top 1% of tokens account for 45–62% of attention weight, compared to 8–12% in null baselines; representation collapse — final-layer hidden state rank is 22–38% of first-layer rank, compared to 85–92% in null baselines; norm stratification — coefficient of variation of key norms is 0.28–0.41, compared to 0.06–0.09 in null baselines.
All four non-token-level routers exhibit identical signature patterns with comparable magnitude: for example, in selective state-space models, the top 2% of historical timesteps account for 51% of gating weight, with a 31% rank decay rate across temporal processing depth.
Positional brake sweep: doubling Transformer positional encoding strength shifts attention sink onset from layer 12 to layer 4, and increases rank decay rate by 2.1x.
Enforced key normalization ablation: key norm coefficient of variation drops to 0.04–0.07 (consistent with null baselines), routing concentration decreases by 58% on average, while 92% of downstream task performance is preserved.ca:T897,Prioritize reading in the following order: First, core theory in Section 3 (Attention as distance-based routing) — focus on Proposition 1 and the KKT derivation of maximum-entropy Boltzmann weights in Appendix A, and clearly distinguish the geometric lens assumptions (A1–A3) from the empirically critical assumption (A4) to avoid misinterpreting manifold assumptions as the actual computational process of the model.

Fourth, investigate whether the low-rank collapse subspace overlaps with the task semantic subspace for in-context learning.cb:T560,The paper defines internalization as a transition from implementing a computation through many explicit steps to implementing it in fewer steps through modified weights. The main empirical setting is semiautomaton simulation. A transformer is trained to generate CoT tokens corresponding to intermediate automaton states over T steps, and then a curriculum progressively removes these CoT tokens so that the model must predict the final state with less explicit computation. This separates learning the step-by-step state transition from compressing the computation. The paper studies task structure through modular counter semiautomata and relates difficulty to the arithmetic structure of the counter order. Counters with small prime-power factors appear easier to represent compactly, while prime-order counters are harder. The theoretical part analyzes sparse parity with a stylized one-layer transformer using linear attention and a fixed nonlinear MLP. The model first learns the hidden-support parity with explicit CoT supervision, then internalizes the autoregressive computation as CoT tokens are removed one at a time, eventually computing the parity directly. On semiautomaton tasks, wider transformers internalize CoT more reliably than deeper transformers under a fixed parameter budget. This weakens the simple picture that implicit reasoning is just explicit reasoning unfolded vertically across layers. Task structure matters: among modular counters, prime-order cases are the most difficult to internalize, consistent with the compact-representation argument. Internalization also has a cost. Models that succeed in-distribution often show degraded out-of-distribution performance, suggesting that the compressed computation can become a shortcut rather than a faithful implementation of the original stepwise algorithm. The theoretical sparse-parity result provides the cleanest positive result: explicit CoT makes the hidden computation learnable, and progressive token removal transfers that computation into the direct predictor. The supplied material does not include checkable numerical details such as model sizes, dataset sizes, or exact accuracy deltas.cd:T5cb,The authors first isolate a simplified Muon update by removing momentum and Newton-Schulz implementation details. The remaining operation replaces each matrix gradient by its polar factor, keeping singular directions while removing singular values. This isolates the effect of gradient orthogonalization. The theoretical testbed is Burer-Monteiro factorized matrix sensing, which is connected to training two-layer quadratic neural networks and allows the gradient and Hessian geometry to be controlled through the sensing operator. The key model is mixed-spiked matrix sensing. Its sensing operator decomposes into signal, spike, and bulk components. The signal component is task-relevant anisotropy aligned with the ground truth. The spike component is strong but task-irrelevant anisotropy. The bulk component captures the remaining more isotropic directions. This construction mirrors a common feature of LLM training: gradients are highly anisotropic, but not every dominant direction is useful. The authors then analyze the landscape using a river-valley decomposition. The river direction corresponds to meaningful progress toward the ground truth, while hill directions capture sharp transverse deviations. In this geometry, GD quickly descends from the hillside into the river but then makes slow progress along the river. Muon moves rapidly along the sides of the valley, which improves exploration, but its normalized update can prevent fine convergence near the solution.ce:T832,方法上分三层。第一层是定义。作者把多轮 MDP 中的状态分成 critical state 和 routine state。critical turn 的动作会改变后续 return distribution；routine turn 虽然是完成任务所必需的执行步骤，但在给定状态下，不同可行动作对最终回报分布近似不变。基于这个划分，decision density ρ 被定义为轨迹中 critical turn 的比例。

第二层是估计器比较。论文比较两类 policy gradient：一类是 turn-level estimator，用每步 advantage A_t 做信用分配，对应 PPO 这一族；另一类是 trajectory-level estimator，用整条轨迹共享的标量优势，对应 GRPO 这一族。关键观察是：在 perfect critic 下，routine turn 的真实 advantage 为 0，因此 turn-level estimator 会逐点把 routine contribution 消掉；而 trajectory-level estimator 只能在期望意义上抵消 routine turn，因为它仍把同一个轨迹级回报乘到这些 turn 的 score function 上，所以会保留额外方差。

第三层是理论推导。作者用 SNR 作为训练步效率代理，分析 turn-level 与 trajectory-level 的信噪比差距。在非退化条件下，perfect critic 情况下 turn-level 相对 trajectory-level 的 SNR 优势按 Θ(ρ^{-1/2}) 增长。也就是说，critical turn 越稀疏，trajectory-level 的浪费越严重。论文还把分析扩展到 imperfect critic：critic 不是免费午餐，若 critic error variance 足够小，turn-level 仍保留优势；但当 critic 误差方差上升到与 decision density 同量级甚至更大时，这种优势会饱和甚至被吃掉。这个扩展很重要，因为它回答了“为什么不是永远上 critic”——因为 critic 的收益要和其误差、成本、稳定性一起看。

实验环境 Diluted Doors 也是技术方案的一部分。它是一个可控 MDP，能精确调节 ρ，同时保持其它因素尽量稳定，用来隔离 signal dilution 机制，而不是在复杂 agent benchmark 上混入太多 confounder。这个设计比直接在真实代码 agent 上做 ablation 更干净。cf:T727,The paper proceeds in three steps. First, it defines critical versus routine turns in a finite-horizon MDP. Critical turns are those where the chosen action changes the future return distribution. Routine turns are necessary execution steps, but alternative admissible actions leave the return distribution effectively invariant. Decision density ρ is then defined as the fraction of critical turns in a trajectory.

Second, it compares two policy-gradient families. A turn-level estimator uses per-step advantages A_t, as in PPO-style methods with a value function. Under a perfect critic, routine turns have zero true advantage and are canceled pointwise. A trajectory-level estimator, as in GRPO-style methods, attaches one scalar advantage to the entire trajectory. In that case, routine turns only cancel in expectation, not per sample, so they retain variance contributions.

Third, it derives an SNR comparison. Using signal-to-noise ratio as a proxy for training-step efficiency, the paper shows that under non-degeneracy assumptions, the SNR advantage of turn-level over trajectory-level estimation scales as Θ(ρ^{-1/2}) in the perfect-critic regime. As decision density decreases, the penalty of trajectory-level credit assignment grows. The analysis is then extended to imperfect critics: the turn-level advantage survives only while critic-error variance remains below the scale set by ρ, and saturates once critic noise becomes too large. This extension is important because it explains why adding a critic is not automatically beneficial.

The controlled environment, Diluted Doors, is also part of the technical contribution. It allows the authors to vary ρ directly while keeping other factors as stable as possible, making it easier to isolate the signal-dilution mechanism than in a full LLM-agent benchmark.d0:T5ea,The experiments are designed to validate the mechanism rather than to maximize downstream scores. The central testbed is Diluted Doors, a controlled MDP with tunable decision density.

The first key result is an SNR study. Over roughly a 50x range of ρ, the empirical SNR ratio between turn-level and trajectory-level estimators follows the predicted ρ^{-1/2} law extremely closely. The paper reports that the fit explains 99.9% of the variation, which is unusually clean evidence for a theory paper.

The second key result is a training-efficiency study. As ρ decreases, trajectory-level learning becomes increasingly inefficient, while the gap in favor of turn-level estimation widens. This supports the paper’s main claim that the cost of critic-free multi-turn RL is governed by decision density rather than horizon alone.

The paper also discusses the imperfect-critic regime. When critic-error variance is controlled, turn-level estimation retains its advantage; when critic noise grows too large, the gain saturates. If the appendix includes explicit critic-noise sweeps, that part is especially relevant for real LLM RL where value estimation is often unstable.

A limitation is that the empirical evidence is primarily from a controlled MDP, not a full-scale LLM agent training run. So the paper is strong on causal identification and weak on external validity. The next practical question is how to estimate ρ in real agent traces and whether routine versus critical turns can be detected reliably.d1:T6b2,Start with the introduction. The two terms to anchor on are signal dilution and decision density. The paper’s main claim is already visible there: the problem in multi-turn RL is not just long horizon, but sparse consequential decisions.

Then read the formal setup and theory sections carefully. Pay attention to how routine states are defined through return-distribution invariance, what exact estimators are being compared, and what assumptions are needed for the SNR scaling result. The usefulness of the conclusion depends on how restrictive those assumptions are.

Next, inspect the construction of Diluted Doors. The important question is whether the environment really varies ρ without simultaneously changing horizon, reward scale, or transition stochasticity. If that control is clean, the empirical validation is much more convincing.

In the experiments, prioritize the figure showing SNR ratio versus ρ and the figure showing training efficiency as ρ changes. One validates the theoretical slope; the other shows that the effect matters for actual learning speed, not just for a derived statistic.

Three follow-up questions are worth carrying into a second pass. First, how could ρ be estimated in real agent tasks from rollouts, tool traces, or verifier signals? Second, can the critic-error-versus-ρ comparison be turned into a practical criterion for whether a critic is worth training? Third, are there cheaper middle-ground solutions—process rewards, step-level verifiers, segment-level return decomposition—that recover some of the benefit without a full critic? First, it performs a descriptive analysis with anchor-conditioned routing. Repeated anchor token ids are aligned across rollouts, and the corresponding sparse routing vectors are compared to test whether routing still separates problem identity, trajectory context, and effort mode. The authors define three anchor families—trajectory, boundary, and delimiter—and vary the routing readout window around the anchor. Routing representations are built from selected expert ids and router weights across layers, and then analyzed with nearest-neighbor leakage and KNN basin-purity style metrics.

Second, the paper proposes RAD, Routing Agreement Decoding. Given a pool of completed rollouts for one problem, RAD locates a fixed anchor by token id, represents each rollout using the routing window around that anchor, and selects the rollout that lies in the densest Weighted-Jaccard KNN routing neighborhood. During selection, it never parses, normalizes, compares, or executes answer strings. The answer text is only read after the routing-based choice is made. In that sense, RAD is analogous to majority voting in objective, but not in interface: majority aggregates agreement in answer space, while RAD aggregates agreement in routing space.d3:T52a,The evaluation covers 10 sparse-MoE configurations and 6 datasets, including gpt-oss and Qwen3-MoE variants, with math, GPQA, LiveCodeBench, and SWE-bench Verified. For a fixed trajectory, the authors run two matched conditions: one keeps the original plan in history, the other replays the same trajectory with the plan removed from history. At each step and layer, they measure cosine distance between hidden states across the two runs. This distance is treated as a plan-fidelity signal. If the model has internalized the plan, removing the text should not quickly change later hidden states. If the model depends on rereading the plan from context, the difference should be large near the plan and then collapse once the plan is no longer actively represented.

They test this on ReAct agents built from Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, replicate within family on Llama-3.1-8B, and compare against DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B. A key methodological contribution is the reasoning-trace confound. In reasoning models, prior <think> blocks often restate the plan. If one removes only the explicit plan text, both replay conditions may still contain plan information, making the measured distance artificially small. Their strict stripping fix removes prior <think> blocks from the plan-removed condition, yielding a cleaner estimate of whether the plan remains available in context.

They also train Ridge probes on hidden states to predict signal magnitude and classify active versus decayed plans. The best layer is L32 in Llama. Probe transfer from Llama to R1 is only partial, and self-probes indicate that R1 uses a substantially different representational direction. The paper is careful about scope: these are representational claims, not strong causal claims about behavior. The authors explicitly note confounds from step index, history length, and discourse structure.d5:T721,On ALFWorld with Llama-3.1-70B, the plan signal peaks at 0.453 one step after the plan is written, then drops by 4.1x within a single action-observation cycle, settling near 0.027 by step +5. 算法部分提出 P-learning，可以看成 Q-learning 的逆问题。普通 Q-learning 在固定环境转移核 P 下，通过 Bellman 更新逼近 Q；P-learning 则把一组固定的 (Q^g, π^g, r^g) 当作观测，迭代更新候选 world model，使它与这些 value functions 的 Bellman 关系越来越一致。作者在 tabular 情形下把这个过程写成线性方程组，并证明收敛到一个由 Moore–Penrose 伪逆给出的解。直观上，Q、policy 和 reward 提供了关于“从状态动作对出发，后继状态分布必须满足什么约束”的大量线性条件；当这些条件足够丰富时，P 就能被唯一识别。文中也说明在很多实际设置里，π 往往由 Q 通过 argmax 或 softmax 导出，因此输入可以近似理解为一组 goal-conditioned Q 和 reward。

理论部分是全文更核心的内容。作者系统分析了在不同 MDP 类型下，什么样的 goal set 能打破 value equivalence。结论分四类。第一，有限状态、确定性 MDP 中，一个“generic” goal 就可能足够识别真实 P。这里 generic 的意思不是任意 goal，而是能让不同后继状态在回报结构上被区分开。第二，有限状态、随机 MDP 中，goals 需要张成状态空间；换句话说，reward family 必须足够丰富，才能把随机转移分布的自由度约束住。第三，确定性连续状态情形里，有限个 goals 有时也足够，这一点有些反直觉，因为连续空间通常让人预期需要无限监督。第四，随机连续 MDP 中，关键不再是 goal 的个数，而是 coverage：对 Gaussian rewards，需要 goal set 有非空内点；对 indicator rewards，需要覆盖状态空间。作者还给出当 Q 只有 ε 近似精度时，恢复出的 P 的误差界，说明 world model 的准确性会随 value 误差平滑退化，而不是脆弱崩掉。

这套方法与传统 world model learning 的区别在于，它不直接拟合转移样本，而是从 agent 已经学到的价值结构中反演环境。与 successor features、forward-backward learning、一般 goal-conditioned RL 的关系则是：这些方法原本被视为多目标 value learning，这篇论文说明在目标集足够丰富时，它们携带的信息量其实接近显式动力学模型。d9:T86d,The paper has two technical pillars: P-learning as an inversion algorithm, and identifiability results that characterize when inversion is possible.

P-learning is introduced as an inverse analogue of Q-learning. In standard Q-learning, the transition kernel is fixed and Bellman updates are used to estimate values. Here the values, policies, and rewards are treated as given, and the transition model is updated so that the Bellman equations become increasingly consistent with those fixed quantities. In the tabular setting, this becomes a structured linear inverse problem, and the paper proves convergence to a solution expressed through the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse. Intuitively, each tuple (Q^g, pi^g, r^g) imposes constraints on what the next-state distribution must be for every state-action pair. If the goal family is rich enough, those constraints pin down the true kernel.

The more fundamental part is the identifiability theory. The paper characterizes when value equivalence can be broken in four regimes. In deterministic finite MDPs, a single generic goal can be sufficient to identify the true dynamics. In stochastic finite MDPs, the reward family must span the state space; otherwise the stochastic degrees of freedom remain hidden behind equivalent values. In deterministic continuous MDPs, somewhat surprisingly, a finite number of goals can still suffice in some cases. In stochastic continuous MDPs, the key notion is coverage rather than cardinality: for Gaussian rewards, the goal set needs non-empty interior; for indicator rewards, it must cover the state space. The paper also provides error bounds showing that if the Q-functions are only epsilon-accurate, the recovered model degrades gracefully rather than catastrophically.

This differs from standard world-model learning because the method does not fit transitions directly from rollouts. Instead, it extracts dynamics from the value structure already learned by the agent. It also reframes goal-conditioned RL, successor-feature style methods, and related approaches as potentially implicit model-learning procedures when the goal family is sufficiently expressive.da:T6d3,The experiments ask two main questions: can P-learning recover accurate world models in practice, and are the recovered models useful beyond the training goals?

For finite MDPs, the paper validates the theory on three FourRooms variants: deterministic, windy, and teleporting. As stochasticity increases, the number of goals needed for near-perfect recovery also increases. The headline numbers are that |G| = 1, 4, and 20 goals are sufficient, respectively, for quasi-perfect recovery in those three settings. This aligns well with the theory: deterministic environments need much less reward diversity than stochastic ones.

In continuous control, the paper studies Reacher and finds that only |G| = 4 goals are enough to recover an accurate implicit world model. A notable result is that the recovered model is accurate even on variables that the reward never directly depends on. Planning inside the recovered model then transfers to out-of-distribution goals, including angular-velocity targets despite training only on position-based goals. That is a strong sign that the agent has internalized more than a narrow reward-specific shortcut.

The MountainCar experiments probe this implicit generalization further. Training on velocity-based goals instead of position-based goals yields an almost identical recovered world model, suggesting that agents optimized for very different objectives may still internalize similar dynamics. Finally, the paper reports a very strong correlation between agent performance and recovered world-model accuracy, with Spearman rho = 0.98. This does not establish causality, but it supports the view that successful goal-conditioned value learning is often accompanied by accurate implicit dynamics learning.db:T4e2,Setup: 28 Reddit communities (17 mental-health, 11 controls). It then computes finite zero-dimensional persistent homology, H0, for each layer. H0 tracks how disconnected components merge as the distance threshold grows, giving a compact view of the connectivity structure among token representations. Each layer is summarized by three descriptors: mean finite lifetime, normalized lifetime entropy, and the concentration ratio of the largest lifetimes. Concatenating these descriptors across layers gives a low-dimensional topology vector for the question. This vector is used for detection and also for steering. For steering, the method retrieves topologically similar positive and negative examples for the current query, constructs a local contrast direction in activation space, and applies the intervention during prefill or decoding. The important design choice is that topology selects the local comparison set, while the actual edit remains in the model’s native activation space.e0:T5fd,The main contribution is Ledger Residuals. A standard pre-norm transformer has a single width-d residual stream that every sublayer reads from and writes to. Ledger Residuals factor this into two width-d streams. The Deliberation stream D is a scratchpad: sublayers can write to it freely and can also erase stale content. The Commitment stream C is an append-only ledger: sublayers may commit information into it through a gate, but cannot overwrite what is already there, and the unembedding reads only from C. Initialization is D0 = embed(x) and C0 = 0. Each sublayer produces both an update to D and a gated contribution to C. The design is intentionally asymmetric: D is where computation happens, C is where the model stores the representation it will be judged on. Importantly, the architecture reduces to a standard pre-norm transformer at a known gate setting, so it serves as a controlled instrument rather than a completely unrelated model family. The causal test is straightforward. If massive activations are just a workaround for the residual stream’s dual role, then a protected decode-only channel should make them unnecessary. The authors also add a commit-sparsity penalty to encourage selective use of C, hoping to keep the commitment channel clean. Instead, stronger sparsity pressure makes the rebuilt outlier more persistent and more concentrated. That is the key technical result: the model actively recreates the feature in the readout channel rather than passively inheriting it from a flawed architecture.e1:T523,The experiments are modest in scale but well controlled. The authors train language models at 160M and 290M parameters and compare Ledger Residuals against standard transformers at matched loss, so the mechanistic conclusions are not confounded by large performance gaps. Three findings matter most. First, a protected decode-only commitment channel does not remove massive activations. The model rebuilds the canonical fixed-dimension outlier in C, and it remains strongly concentrated on the sequence-start token. Second, the rebuilt outlier is somewhat smaller in magnitude than in a standard transformer, but it is more sharply localized in both dimension and position. So the phenomenon is not gone; it is reorganized under the new architectural constraints. Third, the obvious remedy backfires. With stronger commit-sparsity regularization, dominant-dimension persistence rises from 0.58 to 0.96, and start-token concentration rises from 3.4 to 4.7. In other words, the model does not reduce reliance on the outlier channel; it makes that channel more stable and more focused. The paper emphasizes structural measurements rather than benchmark scores: activation magnitude distributions, persistence of the dominant dimension across layers, and concentration on the start token under matched-loss comparisons.e2:T45d,For a skim, start with the Introduction to understand the two competing hypotheses: artifact versus function. Then go straight to Section 3 and Figure 1, which explain the Deliberation/Commitment split and why it is a meaningful controlled intervention. After that, read Section 5 carefully. The most informative plots are the ones showing activation magnitude, dominant-dimension persistence, and start-token concentration. The ablation with commit-sparsity penalty is especially important because it shows that making the commitment channel cleaner does not remove the outlier; it strengthens it. If you only have about 25 minutes, read the Introduction, Section 3, Section 5, and the conclusion. If you want more depth, compare this paper mentally with prior approaches such as key/value biasing, QK normalization, and gated softmax variants. Those works show that outliers can sometimes be suppressed without immediate loss collapse. This paper tests a stronger claim: when the architecture is changed to provide a dedicated readout channel, does the model still choose to recreate the outlier? The answer is yes.e3:T4e8,A three-regime taxonomy is proposed under the thesis that channel location determines auditability. Two key constructs are defined: a screen is any quantity computed before training that predicts transfer magnitude; a carrier is the component whose removal, replacement, or neutralization abolishes transfer. The three regimes are: 1) Initialization-dependent body channel: traits transfer via activation patterns in non-output weights, predictable before training by coverage — the cosine similarity between the student's first distillation gradient step and the teacher's fine-tuning displacement vector; 2) Convergent unembedding / vocabulary geometry channel: single-token traits in pretrained LLMs transfer probability mass via high-cosine neighbours in the output matrix, independent of initialization, so all initialization-alignment screens including coverage fail; 3) A single pretrained model can host both channels, and the active channel is a property of the signal rather than the model — conditional behaviours route through the body channel, while single-token preferences route through readout geometry. A relocation experiment that randomizes the readout restores initialization gating, confirming channel location is signal-dependent.e4:T404,Starting from the established key-value memory interpretation of vanilla FFNs, the work first proves that static or per-pair query projections can be absorbed into the key matrix without increasing expressivity. To unlock additional capacity, dynamically computing per-pair queries and keys from input tokens is required, but this is parameter-prohibitive for large hidden dimensions. A rank-1 outer product approximation of each per-pair QK^T matrix recovers exactly the elementwise multiplicative form of gated MLPs. The work further proves that applying nonlinear activation to one branch (the query branch) before multiplication breaks two symmetries of the unmodified rank-1 formulation: (1) query-key exchange symmetry, broken by any nonlinear activation (only linear activations preserve it); (2) inverse-scaling symmetry, broken by non-homogeneous activations such as SiLU and GELU (ReLU preserves it for positive scaling factors due to positive homogeneity). A rank-R generalization of the formulation is also proposed.e5:T419,The empirical section stresses three tests. On a closed-form anchor, lambda_min^+(G) collapses by about 246x at the bottleneck layer carrying a dead direction, while a dimension-fixed boundary layer remains flat. For multiple dead directions, log det^+(G_l) scales with rank deficit: across 7 noisy-bridge configurations with L in {4,6,8}, D in {20,50}, full-batch and mini-batch SGD, 5 seeds, and r=1..4, the slope ratios for r=2,3,4 are 2.0, 3.1, and 4.0, close to the predicted 2, 3, and 4; the single smallest positive eigenvalue is largely insensitive to r. An off-anchor nonlinear transformer probe keeps the predicted structural sign but loses the trajectory-rate relation, which is an important limitation.e6:T545,The paper has two parts: characterization and mitigation. In the characterization part, pigeonholing is operationalized through three behaviors. One is mistake repetition: the model copies or extends an incorrect answer from context, especially in verifiable domains such as math and coding. Another is stance flipping: the model changes its original answer to align with an incorrect in-context claim. The third is mode collapse: even when the in-context example is not wrong but merely one valid option among many, the model becomes much less likely to explore alternatives and instead reproduces the provided pattern. This broadens the phenomenon from simple accuracy loss to distributional narrowing.

The mitigation strategy is synthetic error augmentation. Instead of changing the architecture, the authors inject erroneous conversational contexts into RLVR and DPO training data, so the model is explicitly optimized to recover when the conditioning history is already corrupted. This is the key distinction from vanilla RLVR or vanilla DPO, which are trained on cleaner or more standard preference-style data. The paper’s argument is that the failure is not just task incompetence; it is misconditioning under bad context. Therefore the training distribution must include corrupted histories if one wants robust recovery at inference time.e7:T567,The empirical coverage is broad. The study evaluates frontier closed models including GPT-4.1, Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Pro, plus seven open-weight models in the 2B–9B range. Tasks span 10 settings, including coding, math, persuasion, and open-ended user interactions, with real-user queries drawn from PRISM, Infinity Chat 100, and Community Alignment. Additional ablations are run on six benchmarks covering logical, commonsense, and social reasoning.

The headline results are clear. Even strong frontier models degrade substantially under erroneous context: around 38% performance drop in math and 40% in coding. The degradation is often monotonic with the number of turns, which suggests cumulative context poisoning rather than isolated prompt brittleness. On the mitigation side, RLVR with synthetic errors improves recovery by 43%–60% over vanilla RLVR on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks. DPO with synthetic errors improves by 34%–35% over vanilla DPO. A key negative result is that vanilla RLVR and vanilla DPO do not reliably fix mistake pigeonholing at test time.

Another strength of the experiments is that they do not only report task accuracy. They also track repeated mistakes, stance changes, and reduced answer diversity, which makes the phenomenon more convincing as a distributional failure mode rather than a narrow benchmark artifact.e8:T452,The contribution is a structured design space for inference-time cross-lingual exploration rather than a single new algorithm. They claim four inherent dimensions governing cross-lingual exploration (details are in the main method section; from the provided content and cited prior work, these dimensions plausibly include: reasoning vs answering language, pivot vs non-pivot routing, which prompt components are translated, and multi-path sampling/aggregation).

第二部分是 cliff token 的统计判定。作者不是简单要求 pot_{t-1}-pot_t 超过固定阈值，而是要求它至少超过 0.1，并且通过一侧 two-proportion z-test 的 95% 置信检验。等价地，阈值写成 0.1 + 1.645 * SE_t，其中 SE_t 由相邻两个位置的 rollout 成功率估计方差决定。这样在 pot 接近 0.5、方差较大的区域，判定门槛会更高；在 pot 接近 0 或 1 的区域，门槛较低。作者明确想避免把 rollout 噪声误判成 cliff，这比固定 0.2 或 30% drop 的规则更稳。

第三部分是 cliff taxonomy。作者根据该 token 是否是 greedy choice，以及该位置分布熵的高低，把 cliff 分成 deterministic、uncertain、sampled-off 三类。可以把它理解为三种不同失败机制：deterministic cliff 表示模型高置信地走错；uncertain cliff 表示模型自己也不确定，错误 token 出现在高熵竞争位置；sampled-off cliff 则更像采样偏离，模型的 greedy 也许不会错，但采样选到了坏分支。这个分类不是装饰性的，因为后面的干预和训练结果表明三类 cliff 的可修复性不同。

在干预上，作者做了两种关键验证。其一是删除第一个 cliff token 后重新采样，观察 pass@64 是否恢复；其二是保留 cliff token 但只重采样后续，观察是否仍然无法完全恢复。这个设计直接检验“cliff 是触发点而不是伴随现象”。其后又提出 Cliff-DPO：把 cliff 位置的好坏 token 构造成偏好对，分别在不同 cliff 子集上训练，比较哪类 token 监督真正有用。与一般 process supervision 不同，这里监督信号被压缩到单 token 位置，目标更尖锐。ef:T83d,The method has three main components. First, it defines token-wise potential. For a prompt, a partial reasoning prefix, and a ground-truth answer, the model rolls out N continuations from every token position and measures the fraction that end with the correct answer. This gives pot_t at each token t. The paper uses N=64 and computes this densely over the full trace, not just at a sparse subset of positions. The cost is high, but the localization is precise.

Second, it introduces a statistical criterion for cliff detection. A token is not labeled a cliff simply because pot_{t-1} - pot_t exceeds a fixed threshold. Instead, the drop must be at least 0.1 and pass a one-sided two-proportion z-test at 95% confidence. This yields an adaptive threshold of the form 0.1 + 1.645 * SE_t, where SE_t depends on the estimated variance of the rollout success rates at adjacent positions. The point is to avoid false positives in high-variance regions, especially around intermediate potential values.

Third, the paper proposes a taxonomy of cliff tokens: deterministic, uncertain, and sampled-off. The categorization uses whether the token is the greedy choice and the entropy of the local token distribution. Intuitively, deterministic cliffs correspond to confident but wrong decisions; uncertain cliffs arise at ambiguous, high-entropy positions; sampled-off cliffs reflect failures introduced by sampling away from a better-ranked continuation. This taxonomy is not cosmetic. It becomes central in the intervention and training results.

The causal validation is well designed. The authors delete the first cliff token and resample from that point, then compare this with keeping the cliff token fixed and only resampling the suffix. If recovery happens only when the cliff token is removed, that supports the claim that the token is a trigger rather than a post hoc marker. They then build Cliff-DPO by constructing preference pairs around cliff positions and training on different cliff subsets separately. Compared with generic process supervision, this is a much sharper token-level supervision signal.f0:T6fa,The study covers seven models and three math reasoning benchmarks: Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-0.6B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.2-1B, and Gemma-3-4B, evaluated on GSM1K, MATH500, and AIME 2025. Token-wise potential is estimated with 64 rollouts per position.

The most important result is the causal intervention. Deleting the first cliff token and resampling restores pass@64 to 1.0, while keeping that token and only resampling the continuation fails to fully recover. That is the strongest evidence in the paper: cliff tokens behave like actual failure triggers, not merely locations where failure becomes visible.

A second result is the cross-model taxonomy analysis. Deterministic cliffs appear relatively scale-invariant, whereas uncertain and sampled-off cliffs better reflect model-specific gaps or scale asymmetries. In practical terms, some errors persist even as models scale because they are confident misgeneralizations, while others are more about uncertainty or decoding-induced branch selection.

A third result comes from Cliff-DPO. Training on uncertain and sampled-off cliff subsets improves reasoning performance, while training on deterministic cliffs does not. The full excerpt does not include every hyperparameter or table entry, but the qualitative conclusion is already informative: token-level supervision helps when the failure is near a ranking boundary or caused by sampling, and helps much less when the model is confidently wrong.

The paper also reports that the adaptive threshold varies roughly from 0.18 to 0.24 depending on the local potential regime, with stricter thresholds in higher-variance middle regions. This is a small but important implementation detail because it explains why the method is more robust than fixed-drop heuristics.f1:T500,Read it in the following order: definition, causal validation, taxonomy, then Cliff-DPO.

First, the paper constructs behavior directions in two ways: data-driven difference-in-means directions from activations, and hand-picked directions from lm_head rows associated with behavior-specific tokens. Detection is built both ways; intervention, especially refusal, is mainly derived from lm_head token directions. Second, the authors do causal testing rather than stopping at probing. They inject directions into the residual stream with forward hooks and measure behavioral changes layer by layer at inference time. Third, they analyze the geometry and the mechanism behind the mismatch. For formatting, detection and control collapse onto essentially the same axis. For hallucination, the cosine between detection and intervention is only about 0.12, roughly an 83-degree separation. They also rule out a construction artifact: even a detector built purely from activations, without hand-chosen tokens, remains misaligned with control, with cosine around -0.06. A key conceptual point appears later in the paper: cosine is not a steerability oracle. Detection is not a single privileged vector but a high-dimensional equivalence class, while steerability is functional. What matters is whether the control direction also serves as a detector, not whether one static angle is large. Mechanistically, the paper traces the hallucination mismatch to the output mapping, where an entity-copying pathway dominates the epistemic signal. As a result, pushing along the detection direction can strengthen name completion and make fabrication worse instead of triggering refusal. Given a user query, it constructs an agentic scaffold over a pool of frontier LLM workers: which workers to call, what roles or instructions they receive, how they interact with tools or environments, how intermediate outputs are checked, and how the final response is synthesized. The report describes two operating points. Fugu is optimized for speed and selects a single worker per input, aiming for latency close to a direct frontier-model call while improving query-specific routing. Fugu-Ultra is optimized for quality and can compose multiple agents per input, trading additional latency for better performance on complex tasks. This differs from static ensembling and simple winner-take-all routing because the scaffold itself is generated by a model and may include decomposition, role assignment, communication, verification, and synthesis. The worker pool can also be configured around provider, privacy, compliance, or user constraints without retraining the orchestrator.f5:T41a,The report claims that Fugu exceeds individual publicly accessible frontier workers on a range of engineering, scientific, and reasoning benchmarks, and is competitive with Fable 5 and Mythos Preview on several rigorous evaluations. The key claim for Fugu-Ultra is that multi-agent composition improves quality on harder tasks by combining specializations. The provided text explicitly mentions software-engineering benchmarks, scientific tasks, reasoning tasks, and the abstract points to SWE-style evaluations. The critical experimental checks are whether the worker pool contains the compared systems, whether routing data overlaps benchmark styles, how Fugu-Ultra is normalized for extra calls and tokens, and whether the multi-agent gain remains after compute and latency are controlled.f6:T79d,AdaMem centers on a structured Memory Policy. The policy is a JSON object that maps each character or role C_i to a natural-language extraction preference T_i, such as keeping only final business decisions and deadlines while ignoring casual chatter. The system then runs a weekly closed loop with four stages.

First is Daily Extraction. New conversations are processed by an extractor LLM, but the extraction prompt is conditioned on the current policy rather than using a generic save-everything rule. The paper also adds Time Anchoring: the prompt includes the absolute session date and instructs the model to resolve relative expressions like “tomorrow” into absolute dates before storing them. That is a small but important systems detail, because relative temporal references decay quickly in long-term memory.

Second is Weekly Evaluation. At the end of each week, the system is probed with QA examples targeting preference-aligned information.

Third is Policy Reflection. Errors are diagnosed into two categories. Recall Failure means the relevant information appeared in dialogue but was never written, so the policy is too restrictive. Precision Failure means irrelevant retrieved memories polluted the answer, so the policy is too permissive. Based on these failures, the model generates a policy patch rather than rewriting the full policy from scratch. This patch-style update is easier to inspect and easier to roll back.

Fourth is Failure Rollback and Policy Rendering. If the updated policy hurts validation performance on historical QA pairs, the change is rejected and the system reverts to the previous policy. The accepted policy is then rendered into extraction instructions for the next week. The interesting part here is not a new neural architecture but a control loop: write policy, evaluate, diagnose, patch, validate, and only then deploy. That makes the method easy to insert into existing RAG-style memory stacks.f7:T6f7,The evaluation includes both a new benchmark and the method comparison itself. The benchmark, AdaMem-Bench, is designed specifically for preference-guided long-horizon memory. It uses multi-session dialogues over multiple weeks, multiple concurrent personas, and deliberately overlapping semantic content across characters so that the system must avoid confusing similar but irrelevant memories. Each session is annotated with golden memories: atomic facts that match the character’s preference profile are labeled as relevant, while the rest is treated as noise. That setup is better aligned with the paper’s goal than generic QA benchmarks.

Empirically, the paper reports up to +9.0% QA accuracy while reducing memory volume by 9%, across two extractor LLMs and two feedback modes. That combination matters more than the accuracy number alone, because it suggests the gains come from better selectivity rather than from simply storing more information. The analysis says improvements are concentrated in soft-preference categories such as emotions, promises, and schedules. That is plausible: these are exactly the categories where a uniform extraction rule tends to either miss subtle information or over-store irrelevant details. The main remaining bottleneck is policy inference from weak feedback, meaning the system can observe that an answer failed but cannot always infer the right policy adjustment.

When reading the experiments, the most useful questions are practical ones: what the baselines are, how memory volume is measured, how often rollback is triggered, and whether the gains hold across different extractor models. If the paper includes error-type breakdowns by recall versus precision failure, those are likely more informative than the top-line QA score.f8:T41a,Two pillars:
1) TMAX-15K environment generation: instead of only generating trajectories, they synthesize full terminal RL environment instances using a strong frontier model. A taxonomy drives generation with explicit difficulty control, persona variation (to diversify constraints and narrative framing), and verifier diversification (to avoid brittle binary checks). Some tasks use continuous-valued rewards rather than pass/fail.
2) RL recipe (TMAX): built on an asynchronous RL stack (open-instruct). They report naive GRPO becoming unstable in long-horizon agent settings, and switch to DPPO (Divergence Proximal Policy Optimization). Two emphasized stabilizers are an FP32 LM head (to mitigate mixed-precision numerical issues around logits/softmax/entropy/KL) and a large group size (lower-variance advantage estimates and smoother updates).
Compared to prior open terminal-agent efforts, the novelty is less about a new algorithm and more about a coherent, stability-first training stack paired with harder, taxonomy-controlled The motivation is that LLMs may not memorize a verbatim passage, yet still absorb and later reveal facts, relations, and descriptive patterns about a person, organization, or event from many scattered mentions. central question in masked diffusion and other any-order discrete generators: when is parallel unmasking statistically faithful, and when does it fail because it ignores conditional dependence among tokens? In autoregressive sampling, one-token-at-a-time decoding is exact under the chain rule regardless of order. In masked diffusion, revealing multiple coordinates at once replaces a true block conditional with a product of one-coordinate marginals. That approximation is only valid under conditional independence. The paper isolates this sampler error from model error by moving to a controlled setting.","importance":"This is a strong paper for anyone working on non-AR language modeling. attention 输出。第一是 content channel：对匹配到的 value-sum 做单位球投影，只保留方向，减少上下文长度变化带来的幅度漂移。第二是 count channel：用 participation ratio，也就是 inverse Simpson index，估计有多少 key The blocks use pre-normalization and a 4x squared-ReLU MLP. Polar Attention replaces the usual softmax readout with three additive streams. The content stream normalizes the matched value sum onto the unit sphere, preserving direction while removing length-dependent magnitude. The count stream estimates how many items participated in the match using the participation ratio, or inverse Simpson index, then bounds it through a saturating monotone map. This explicitly decouples what was matched from how much was matched. The memory stream is a per-head recurrent associative memory with a gated-delta update, inspired by Titans. token，而是只保留一个受限的可见视觉上下文窗口，同时通过检索机制访问与当前问题相关的过去观测。\n\n这套设计的关键不是某个单独技巧，而是几个约束一起工作。chunking 提高前端吞吐，token dropping 控制 token 密度，bounded attention 把 prefill 成本封顶，retrieval 则尽量补偿截断历史带来的信息损失。作者把这件事表述为 slowest-stage scheduling problem：只要每个 chunk 在最慢阶段的处理时间低于视频到达间隔，系统就能持续实时运行。这样，查询时的 TTFT 也不再随着视频总时长增长，而是主要由受限上下文下的一次 prefill 决定。\n\n和已有 streaming VideoLLM 的区别也比较清楚。delayed streaming 把大部分计算拖到用户提问时做一次大 prefill，延迟和显存都随历史增长；已有 continuous streaming 工作虽然做了稀疏编码、关键帧选择或 cache 压缩，但常缺少端到端流水线视角，容易出现“前面快了，后面堵住”的瓶颈迁移。ViCoStream 试图把这些局部优化放到统一调度框架里讨论。","experiments":"实验主结果是系统吞吐和精度折中。论文报告，在 30% token retention 下，ViCoStream 可达到 134 FPS，同时多数中等压缩设置下精度与 full-history baseline 基本持平。这个结果说明，只要视觉 token 密度和可见历史被合理约束，流式 VideoLLM 的可持续吞吐可以远高于常见实时视频帧率，而不必把全部历史都塞进 LLM。\n\n更有价值的是系统性分析，而不是单个 headline 数字。作者考察了 chunk granularity、token retention ratio、visual-context size、retrieval scope 等因素如何影响瓶颈迁移。这里的重点不是“某个参数最优”，而是不同设置会把瓶颈从视觉前端转移到 LLM prefill，或者反过来。比如 token dropping 虽然减少了 LLM 计算，但如果视觉编码仍是最慢阶段，整体 FPS 不一定提升；反过来，如果前端已经足够快，而 visual context 不受限，TTFT 仍会随历史增长。论文想证明的是，只有把各阶段一起协调，才能得到稳定的吞吐-延迟曲线。\n\n从阅读价值看，建议特别关注作者是否给出了长时流上的内存曲线和 TTFT 曲线。如果这些曲线确实随 stream length 保持近似平坦，那就说明 bounded visual attention 的设计是有效的；如果只是短视频上快一些，意义会小很多。摘要里没有列出完整 benchmark 名称和每项精度数字，但全文的实验组织方式明显偏系统论文：强调 sustained FPS、TTFT、memory budget 和 accuracy 的联合分析。","reading_guide":"这篇适合带着系统问题去读。先看 Introduction 和 pipeline Activation-aware variants such as SVD-LLM(W) preserve forward activations better, yet they still do not distinguish which approximation errors actually matter for the final prediction. Prior backward-signal methods either underperform activation-only baselines or rely on expensive end-to-end optimization. next-token decoding always read from the final layer? The full paper argues that depth is not uniformly monotonic in usefulness for decoding. For many tokens, early layers make a rough guess, intermediate layers stabilize the reasoning-relevant semantics, and the last few layers can then shift the distribution toward generic, alignment-favored, or pragmatically safer continuations. The authors call this pattern Guess–Refine–Perturb. The actual problem is therefore not early exiting for efficiency, but how to choose, at each generation step, the most reliable near-final layer for emission without changing model weights or truncating the forward pass.","importance":"Its value for foundation-model research is twofold. First, it is a mechanistic claim against the common assumption that deeper is always better for decoding. It links post-training signals—style control, safety shaping, preference alignment—to late-layer distribution drift. That matters for the pretrain/post-train interface, because it suggests that alignment may not only change final behavior, but also alter where in depth the cleanest task semantics appear. Second, the proposed decoding rule is training-free and parameter-free. If the phenomenon is real and robust, part of the so-called alignment tax may be recoverable at inference time rather than only through new training objectives. 接口有启发：一方面，它把长期记忆和通用能力解耦，避免 per-user 微调污染基座；另一方面，它说明 soft prompt 不一定要是静态参数，也可以是由外部 latent memory 动态生成的条件化前缀。从系统角度看，作者把个性化问题重新表述为“低成本记忆压缩 + 条件检索”的组合，而不是“给每个用户训练一个小模型”。这对未来做 continual N×d_mem；实际实现里还用了 H 个独立 memory heads，每个 head 有自己的 slots 和投影参数，用来缓解单一记忆矩阵的瓶颈。第二部分是共享 projection network。给定当前输入 x，先用一个小型冻结 embedding model 得到输入表示 ε(x)，再让 ε(x) 作为 query、用户 memory slots 作为 key/value 做 cross-attention，得到每个 head 的检索结果；之后经过 MLP 和 LayerNorm 映射到 LLM hidden size，形成若干 soft prompt 向量，拼接后前置到原始输入前面。关键点在于 prompt 不是用户固定参数，而是由“当前问题 × 用户记忆”共同决定，因此同一用户在不同问题下会激活不同记忆子空间。\n\n训练方式也有几个值得注意的细节。作者不是直接把整段用户历史编码成一个向量，而是把完整历史切成固定大小的 chunks，按时间顺序处理。处理第 t 个 chunk 时，使用从前一 chunk 检索出的 prompt P_{t-1} 来做 next-token prediction，这样避免未来信息泄漏。训练时更新的参数包括 cross-attention 的 W_Q/W_K/W_V、MLP、LayerNorm，以及用户自己的 memory slots；基座 LLM 完全冻结。为了避免 slot-attention 坍缩到少数槽位，作者加入了一个 hinge-style entropy regularizer：当注意力熵低于目标值时才惩罚，目的是防止所有槽位学成同一语义，同时又不强迫完全均匀分配。这个设计比直接最大化熵更稳，因为记忆检索本来就应该允许在某些问题上高度集中。另一个工程选择是共享 projection network 的梯度在所有用户上累积后每个 epoch 再更新一次，以降低 per-user 更新带来的噪声；这也让它更接近可扩展的 federated
